A1.justification: Both 31-page PDFs describe the same FIRE/DDfire work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original FFHQ and ImageNet reconstruction experiments, ablations, runtime comparisons, and appendix analyses of tuning and variance estimation.

after.justification: v4 retains the original reconstruction experiments, ablations, runtime results, and supplementary analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The SLM/GLM-FIRE, DDIM integration, and guidance procedures are retained. Algorithms 2 and 7 explicitly list the likelihood as an alternative input, clarifying existing GLM support. The equation corrections repair the existing mathematical construction.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FFHQ and ImageNet on box inpainting, Gaussian and motion deblurring, 4× super-resolution, and OSF/CDP phase retrieval. No evaluated dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same per-task comparators. DDRM remains absent from motion deblurring; phase retrieval retains HIO, DOLPH, DPS, RED-diff, DAPS, and prDeep.

E3.justification: Section 4 replaces the blanket 800-NFE phase-retrieval setting with 800 for OSF and 100 for CDP. Appendix H.4 already specified those separate budgets in v3, so this corrects a reported inconsistency without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Section 4 adds a brief iteration-budget sensitivity report: further CDP steps offered no improvement. No quantitative sweep accompanies it. Table 1’s ablations and the existing appendix sensitivity, variance-tracking, and runtime analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix H.2 retains four OSF runs with residual-based selection and single runs for linear problems and CDP. The tuning-curve error bars in Figures 7–10 and other statistical reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical benchmark results and reconstruction images are unchanged, including Table 4’s DDfire CDP PSNR values of 30.16 and 28.91. The only added qualitative finding is that further CDP NFEs offered no improvement.

T1.justification: Equation (13) restores the missing A in A^T[Ax0 + sigma_y w]. Appendix D’s Equation (64) replaces s_i with s_max inside the scalar renoising coefficient. Theorem 1 and its proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning colored renoising, convergence, the EP extension, DDIM integration, and reconstruction accuracy/runtime.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly justifies the existing 100-NFE CDP budget through the reported lack of improvement from further steps. Other mechanism explanations, CG tradeoffs, and the appendix qualification about hyperparameter sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H.4 replaces the promise of code release upon acceptance with an availability statement at the repository already listed in v3’s abstract. This resolves inconsistent access documentation without establishing newly available code.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive comparisons with prior methods are retained. Meng and Kabashima (2024) remains in the bibliography and its method remains discussed, although its in-text citation becomes an unresolved question mark.

P1.justification: v4 makes limited wording, punctuation, and author-contact edits and adds acknowledgements. It also introduces an unresolved citation in Section 3.4 and substitutes 'stochastic damping' in Section 4, inconsistent with the retained stochastic-denoising description.

P2.justification: v4 adds publication headers and an OpenReview line and reflows text, tables, and references. Table 2 moves from page 10 to page 11. The figures and tables retain their visual content and design.

improvement.justification: Repairing Equations (13) and (64) and reconciling Section 4’s CDP budget with Appendix H.4 improve mathematical and experimental clarity. These limited gains outweigh the new broken citation and inconsistent damping terminology. The numerical evidence and core method remain stable.
